label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Thursday's launch (DRAFT, not yet shared)

Inês,

Thank you for taking this on. I am sorry to leave it to you like this. My father is ill and I am with my family, and I don't know yet how long I'll be away. I found the error in figure 3 only this afternoon, so you are inheriting a real problem, not just a run of show. Everything is in this folder and in my inbox, but this page is the order I would work in.

The short version: the paper's conclusion is unchanged, but the headline 2030 number is wrong in some places. The correct figure is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The error is mine, from the old run where the free allocation phase-out was not applied. If anyone asks, say so plainly. It is my mistake, not yours.

What is already out there

Hanna sent the press release to our 34 Brussels contacts on Friday, under embargo until Thursday 26 November at 10:00 CET. It says 2.1 billion. It has to be corrected before the embargo lifts. Hanna should send a corrected version to the same list, clearly marked as a correction, ideally by Wednesday. If she wants a senior name on it, Geert knows I am away and has agreed to sign off a corrected release. Please talk to him directly.

Two journalists asked for calls before the event, one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. Hanna said I would be available on Wednesday afternoon. My calendar has two 20-minute background calls on Wednesday 25 November, at 14:00 and 15:00, with Hanna still to confirm. If Hanna cannot confirm them, ask her to move them. If they go ahead, please take them, or sit in with Hanna. Both journalists will ask about the number, so tell them the correct figure of EUR 1.4 billion and that the earlier release was wrong.

What to do, in order

1. Tonight or tomorrow morning: check that Hanna has the corrected release ready, and that she knows about the Wednesday calls. Geert can sign off if needed.

2. By Wednesday 25 November at 12:00 at the latest: send Tomás Reyes (tomas.reyes@ep-office-lindqvist.example) the final names of everyone coming from our side, or security will not let them in. You will be there. I may already have sent this from the train tonight, but please check. If I have not, please send it yourself, with your name and anyone else from our side.

3. Fix the deck (v4) before anything else goes out. Slides 6 and 9 still use the old number. Slide 9 has the revenue chart, so the chart data needs to change, not just the label. Use the corrected figure from PDF v7 on the drive, which has the right number on pages 3, 14 and 15. Check my speaker notes in the deck too, since they may still say 2.1. You shortened the deck well, so keep it at 14 slides.

4. Check the remote link for Dr. Abena Owusu-Mensah on Thursday morning. You tested it on Tuesday and it worked, but test again before the room fills.

5. Check the Thursday timings with Tomás on Wednesday. The MEP has a vote moved into Thursday lunchtime and must leave at 13:30. The changes are:
- Welcome by Lindqvist at 12:30, 5 minutes.
- Your presentation at 12:35, now 15 minutes, not 20, so it ends at about 12:50.
- Panel starts at 12:50, not 12:55. Panel is Abena (remote), Florian Kessler of the Alliance of European Steel Users, and you. Lindqvist moderates and wants to take at least two questions herself before 13:30.
- The 13:40 Q&A will not happen in the usual form, because Lindqvist will be gone. Ask Tomás on Wednesday who chairs the rest of the session and who closes it, instead of the 14:00 close as planned.

Guests should be at security by 12:00. Light lunch is outside the room from 12:00.

6. Kessler: he will raise the 80% pass-through assumption in section 4 and the resource shuffling risk. He wrote to me on 12 November, and his members say pass-through is much lower for small manufacturers. Be open about it and do not get defensive. The 80% is our central case. Annex B, which you ran yourself, tests 40% and 60%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say that clearly if he pushes. On resource shuffling, we agree it is a risk. It is discussed in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report. Do not let him set the tone of the session. You know this paper as well as I do.

Abena will probably back us on the LDC side. She was strong on the call with us.

7. After the event: Lucy Tran at the Halvorsen Foundation is attending with a colleague. For the grant report she needs two photos from the event and the attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please send these once the event is over.

Contacts

Geert Lammens can sign off the corrected press release and can make decisions about the launch. Hanna Weber handles press and the embargo. Tomás Reyes is the MEP's office for badges and timings. You can call me. After 9 tomorrow morning I may not be able to pick up, so if something is urgent after that, go to Geert first.

What you already know

You ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself, so you know the weak points better than anyone. At the COP side event in Lisbon, when the projector died, you kept the panel going, and you did it well. You are better live than you think. Lindqvist's office and the panel will see that on Thursday.

I trust you completely with this. I know it is not how I wanted to hand this over, and I am sorry for the error and for leaving you with it. Thank you for doing it.

Marieke

reasons: The draft says Inês tested Abena’s link on Tuesday, but her 19 November note says she tested it the previous day, Wednesday.
